topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the overarching concepts to be covered regarding immune activation and resolution.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles governing how the innate immune system detects microbes and tissue damage using pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: PRR families, signaling pathways, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific classes of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling mechanisms, and the activation of inflammatory cascades via the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator release, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how innate recognition triggers local leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic drainage, and systemic inflammatory consequences.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms required to terminate inflammation, facilitate tissue repair, and manage unresolved infections through chronic responses or granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic.
